name: FileSystem
intent: A file system over records that live somewhere else. Nodes are a flat array with `parentId`, and each file carries an opaque `ref` the host reads back, so the widget addresses a product's records without holding any of them. File types — their labels, marks and tints — are declared by the host, so it knows no product's vocabulary. It renders two layouts: a flat listing of every project and file under the root, narrowed by type / project / tag facets down the left with a search band spanning both, and a project's own page with Overview / Files / Trash sections and folders you can open. A row never navigates — clicking one selects it and a details panel answers what it is — while the underlined name is the only thing that leaves, and a `New` menu adds projects, folders and files. It owns no data: nodes go in as a prop and creation comes back out through `onCreate`, so the host keeps them wherever the rest of its state lives.
when: Giving records that live in several different apps one address each, and one place to browse them
A listing whose reader asks 'what is this?' as often as 'take me there' — the row selects, the name navigates
Browsing by type, project or tag rather than by walking a folder tree
A product that already owns its records and needs the naming layer, not another store
whenNot: Browsing a real filesystem or an object store -> this addresses records, and holds no bytes
One flat list with no hierarchy and no facets -> use DataTable
Picking a single file inside a form -> use CanvasFilePicker
Navigating an app's own sections -> use SideMenu or CoreAppSidebar

chooseOver.because: DataTable lists rows. FileSystem adds the hierarchy around them — projects, folders, paths, facets and a details panel — and the two-target row that separates selecting from leaving.
SideMenu navigates an app's own sections. FileSystem navigates the records those apps own, from outside all of them.

allowedPlacement: a route-level surface, or any column that gives it height

extracted: the whole surface, which shipped inside the template first and was lifted out once it was clear nothing in it was Core-specific
the model — index, queries, facets, tag inheritance — which is pure and takes an index rather than reading a fixture

lineage.confidence: unset — extracted from a prototype, no held-out eval yet
notes: Holds NO data. `nodes` is a prop and `onCreate` returns the created node, so the host decides where the array lives — module state, a store, a server. The widget derives its indexes with useMemo and nothing else.
Knows no product's vocabulary. `fileTypes` declares the labels, icons, tints and owning apps; a node names a type by id, and `ref` is `unknown` — handed back to the host and never read here.

Two targets in one row: the ROW selects into the details panel, the underlined NAME leaves. Selecting and leaving are different intentions, and a row that navigated on click would make 'what is this?' impossible to ask without losing your place to answer it.

Facets, not a tree. A folder tree was built first and removed: it repeated the path already printed under every row, cost the widest column on the surface, and could not answer the question the list is actually asked ('show me the pipelines').
Folders ARE navigable inside a project, where the question is 'what is in here?' rather than 'where is this?'. The flat listing never shows one.

Tags inherit: a file matches its own tags plus every tag on the project and folders above it, so a project tagged for a region makes its files findable under it. Facet counts and query matches come from the same function, so a facet can never offer a value that finds nothing.

The project page ships Overview / Files / Trash — the sections a file system can fill from its own data. A host wanting a cover page or a usage report should compose them around the widget rather than have it ship empty shells.
Rename and move are not implemented.
